definition.simple: Atoms of the SAME element that have a DIFFERENT weight because they have extra neutrons.
definition.academic: Two or more forms of the same element that contain equal numbers of protons but different numbers of neutrons in their nuclei, and hence differ in relative atomic mass but not in chemical properties.

examples: Carbon-12 and Carbon-14 are both carbon, but Carbon-14 is heavier.
Chlorine has two isotopes with mass 35 and 37.

common_misconceptions: Isotopes behave differently in chemical reactions. (False: They have the same electrons, so they react exactly the same).
ai_context.tutor_hint: To remember Isotopes vs Isobars: IsoTOPES have the same 'P' (Protons/atomic number) but different masses.
